title: Turrican II: The Final Fight
build: Triangle disk release from the C64Games archive

records.c: Type three initializes health one, facing toward the player and a six-update four-shape animation. Its ordinary movement turns at solid terrain and follows a thirteen-entry fall curve. A flash-related timer selects the twenty-seven-entry flattened/jump curve. Close player contact either damages the player or enters a delayed flattened state with a 500-point request, depending on jump height and direction. Flattened state later slides left and falls until solid terrain or bounds end it.
Operand byte 1 of the BPL instruction at $6C02, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.

Restore the normal colour or retained hit-flash nibble. Handle flattened state separately. Contact can select flattening before ordinary character damage; surviving hits flash, while accepted destruction requests 100 points. Choose falling, walking or extended-curve states from terrain and the resident flash countdown.
While the curve index is nonnegative, apply its signed Y increment. A downward segment that meets solid terrain sets the index negative and ends further curve motion.

Wait eighteen calls before toggling flattened shapes and following the twenty-seven-entry curve. After it ends, derive a new screen pointer, test the next terrain cells, slide left two half-pixels and fall three pixels when unsupported.
Two facing-specific bases for four walking shapes.
Signed horizontal increments minus/plus one.
Thirteen signed Y increments for ordinary falling.
Twenty-seven signed Y increments used by the flash-related state and flattened movement.

Type four reserves two free slots or releases its source, then initializes three linked pieces. Their source releases all three on bounds. Visible intervals allow player contact, colour cycling and piece-specific XOR shapes; hidden intervals use $FE. The final hidden tick restores the piece shape and requests a sound on the third channel.
Three linked-piece shapes.
Three source-relative half-pixel X offsets.
Three source-relative pixel Y offsets.
Three initial appearance delays.
Three piece-specific XOR animation masks.
Four cyclic visible colours.
Visible/hidden phase durations.

Type five reserves a second slot and initializes two vertically separated pieces. The source state is zero and skips its update; the state-one partner stores the source slot, owns health $20 and updates a twenty-six-entry vertical curve. Contact, protection-dependent character damage, flash destruction or bounds affect both linked slots; destruction requests 500 points.

Share colour/flash state with the linked piece. Player contact damages the player or subtracts a fixed protected-contact amount. Character hits subtract the resident indexed damage. Counter underflow or flash explodes both pieces; bounds release both; otherwise move the active partner through its vertical curve.
Twenty-six signed Y increments for the active linked partner.

Type six allows one linked group, reserves three free slots and builds a two-by-two body with shared health $20. The controller scans up to five screen rows for two-cell character hits, consumes them, handles protected contact and changes its motion state after a surviving hit. A three-pose shape animation spans all four slots. Horizontal terrain reverses facing; a ground probe starts a twenty-entry jump curve. Bounds release the group and destruction requests 2000 points.

Restore four piece colours and test contact before deriving the body screen pointer. Scan five two-cell rows for character damage, updating the shared counter and hit state. Animate three poses, move horizontally by signed facing, and copy four relative positions from the controller's origin.
Four relative half-pixel X offsets.
Four relative pixel Y offsets.
Controller state one followed by three passive state-zero pieces.
Four initial body shapes.
Four piece colours.
Two signed facing increments.
Twenty signed Y increments indexed by the controller jump timer.
Four groups of three animation shapes, one per body piece.
Byte offset 3 in four part pose shapes at $7320-$732B. Four groups of three animation shapes, one per body piece.
Byte offset 6 in four part pose shapes at $7320-$732B. Four groups of three animation shapes, one per body piece.
Byte offset 9 in four part pose shapes at $7320-$732B. Four groups of three animation shapes, one per body piece.

Type seven selects one of two initial shapes/vertical offsets, counter eight, and a forty-call initial wait. After the wait, animate four shapes and emit resident projectile actors at a direction-dependent interval. Signed projectile velocity combines CIA timer bits with subtype base speeds. Destruction requests 250 points.
Two subtype initial shapes.
Two signed base velocities combined with timer bits.
Two subtype initial Y offsets.

Type eight initializes facing and can allocate a linked state-two carried actor beneath it. Ordinary states animate four facing-dependent shapes and move with a sixteen-entry Y curve. The carried state follows its parent until its type changes or an exact horizontal distance is reached; it then falls. Ground contact converts it to a type-seven emitter with reloaded health, delay and position. Destruction requests subtype-selected BCD score fractions.
Four right-facing animation shapes.
Four left-facing animation shapes.
Signed half-pixel movement by facing.
Four BCD fractional score bytes paired with the fixed hundreds amount.
Sixteen signed vertical increments for ordinary movement.

Type nine initializes health twenty in state fourteen and per-slot player-contact flags. Its first weapon hit opens the shape/state before subsequent damage is accepted. Contact near its top supports player Y; deeper contact triggers a nine-entry bump curve, sound and one counter decrement. Aggregate slot flags update resident support bytes $62/$63. Destruction requests 5000 points and fills free slots with timer/code-byte-mixed particles; those move and reflect velocities on terrain before becoming resident effects.

Clear support flags, record the source origin and initialize free slots as type-nine particles with random effect shapes, signed velocities and lifetimes. Use the CIA timer, indexed program bytes and local accumulator, then explode the source and request 5000 points.
Move signed X/Y velocities within bounds and lifetime, switching to resident effect type when either ends. Sample upper/lower and left/right terrain cells to reverse the corresponding speed.
Nine signed Y increments used by support contact.
Copy thirty-two environment bitmap bytes into $C588, set four terrain properties at $BE42 to four and install eight further overrides from $AB60. Continue directly into the update callback.

Animate environment glyphs through the direction table unless halted. At the selected camera rectangle and grounded player state, suppress selected glyph scrolling and allocate a fixed slot-ten boss controller when none is active. A later exact camera column and player threshold select ordinary exit. Animate two ten-glyph groups from three eighty-byte frames each, provide a character-specific rightward player adjustment when controls permit, and rotate two small glyph fragments.

Two independent four-update dividers select one of three eighty-byte frames and copy them into $C008 and $C058. Then apply the conditional player adjustment and bit rotations to glyph fragments at $C1B0/$C1E4.
Unless suppressed, cyclically rotate two sixteen-byte glyph columns upward by two bytes, preserving their wrapped ends.
Unless suppressed, rotate both glyph columns downward by two bytes and wrap their saved ends.

Apply left rotation and conditional downward rotation.
Apply right rotation and conditional upward rotation.
Apply right rotation and conditional downward rotation.
Nine glyph-scroll callback low bytes.
Nine matching high bytes.

Type fifteen installs four-column four-band raster callbacks and counter forty, initializes the body from the actor Y coordinate and releases other ordinary actors. Subsequent calls restore any exchanged bitmap rows, restore default colours and test player contact and weapon-character damage before preparing the next raster.

Complete the boss callback installation, then initialize the forty-count counter, four X columns and four Y bands before clearing other active actors. This program byte is also sampled by the destruction randomizer.

Move the four X columns left one pixel, or two for camera direction four, clearing other nonzero camera directions. On a twenty-one-call divider cycle four poses, replacing two bands of shape/bitmap matrices and adding the selected Y increment to all four band coordinates.

Convert body origin to half-pixel X and test three rectangles. During wheel mode, install an upward-left knockback player callback and sound; otherwise invoke resident player damage when protection is clear. Skip contact effects during the end-of-frame flag.

Release the controller at exact half-pixel X $DA. Otherwise scan ten character rows using two offset columns with adjacent cells each. Consume characters $C8 and above by writing $FF and subtract their resident damage amount from the byte counter. Underflow starts destruction, fills actor slots with explosions, restores the ordinary raster and requests 10000 points.

Replace the accepted screen hit with $FF, subtract its indexed damage and branch to destruction on counter underflow. A byte in this instruction sequence is also sampled by the destruction randomizer.
Request shared flash and fill all eleven actor slots with explosion states at timer/code-byte-mixed positions. Initialize flash timing, request 10000 points and restore the saved raster callback.
Cycle four two-shape player frames while moving up three pixels and left four half-pixels. X wrap past $F0 places the player below the playfield and restores its saved movement callback.

When the nested-frame flag permits, update body movement. Install first-band Y, four shape pointers in both screens, four X coordinates/high-X bits and colours. Set raster timing and enable multicolour on the reused sprites.

Draw four shape/colour entries for the current band, restore pending exchanged rows, advance to the next of four bands and schedule its Y/raster line. At fine-scroll collisions call the twelve-byte bitmap-row substitution helper before returning to the shared IRQ exit.
